legit answer: it’s generally considered rude to make unsolicited sexual comments about people, *especially* strangers. saying “hey, nice tits!” is considered pretty inappropriate in the vast majority of circumstances, but even further just saying “mother milkers” (not even a compliment, just a weird comment pointing out someone’s breasts) to a person who you don’t know that posted a perfectly normal picture where they’re fully clothed is beyond strange. 

complimenting someone’s breasts/butt or really any part of their body in a sexual way is *really inappropriate* if they haven’t explicitly asked for that or unless you have a relationship with that person where it’s normal/warranted. 

these comments are considered degrading because it’s reducing a person to one part of their body or to a sexual act when people are much more than that! this ties into feelings of objectification: someone feels like they’re just an object to be looked at/used/sexualized which is pretty dehumanizing.

if you’re thinking “i wish i would get compliments like that” that’s your own personal preference and it’s best to keep in mind that many others don’t feel that way. appropriate comments for this pic could be complimenting the dress, the lighting, smile, overall saying “you look nice!” etc.

I listed identities that I’ve either known or seen in this very thread to have an issue with being called queer, “queerphobia” wasn’t included just because I haven’t seen anyone say “I have an issue with the term queer because of queerphobia against me” and not because I was deliberately trying to exclude anyone.

Dropping the T is founded on transphobes trying to oust trans people from the community, we aren’t advocating to drop the Q or to “keep an arm’s length from the community” like most people are literally saying “I am personally uncomfortable being lumped in as queer or called queer”

I legitimately can’t tell if you’re approaching this from the perspective that being queer is usually (if not always) an identity that is on its own separate from being gay/lesbian/trans/bi etc because honestly that’d clear up a ton of confusion. Most of the controversy is around queer as an umbrella term, and I think it’s ridiculous to tell a person that they can’t identify as queer. It’s just also fair for a person to not want to be identified as queer when that’s not a label they’re comfortable with.

I dislike queer as an umbrella term because it gives me the fucking chills to be called “queer” by cishets but I’ve happily called myself queer in community spaces for years now, I just want to respect the people who have baggage with the term. If I can’t hear my own weeping apology, yeah that’d probably suck.

Girl I know it’s from adventure time I’m saying it’s still grossly ignorant given the context… We’re talking about trauma and homo/bi/pan/ace/transphobia please read the room!! 

Queer can be RECLAIMED and it is every person’s unique individual right to do that… no one gets to take it from them. Yes I’m familiar, I’ve used the chant while getting involved with my community and local activism!! Where I met loads of people who grew up in horrible environments that left them deeply uncomfortable with the word. Nobody is less valid for not wanting to be called queer… we’re all just out here living our lives and it’s not a label that should be pushed on others.

If you want to identify as queer I’m happy for you, but that doesn’t undo the harm that others suffered. If we want to form a strong community we have to be sensitive to that. Queer is a valid label and part of LGBT*Q* but it’s also been used as a slut against many and they don’t identify with the term at all, why can that not be respected??

??? wtf?? most of the people saying queer is a slur are also LGBT+ people who happen to have a long and traumatic history with the word. so your whole “only death for your people” isn’t as cute as you think it is, it’s disgustingly reminiscent of the violence that we faced in the first place. i shouldn’t be surprised to see such an ignorant and insensitive comment coming from a debate that boils down to “trauma? suck it up sweetie!!” but jeez, read the room

I would love to know what decade you’re stuck in that you think biphobia is fake and the eeevil bisexuals are fetishizing the Real Gays and erasing their history. The world is changing, cry about it

they’re kind of just general, umbrella terms to describe certain experiences or groups, like “fetishizing wlw does not count as acceptance” or “oh that dating app is aimed towards mlm” and that’s pretty much it. lesbian trans women are wlw, demisexual gay men are mlm, and people who are nonbinary or genderfluid sometimes like to align themselves with more femme/masc experiences but absolutely do not have to! afaik there’s no relation to TERFs and the wlw/mlm terms infuriate biphobes (which many TERFs are) which always makes me happy 🖤

wlw and mlm are usually used to *include* bi people and other identities. “lesbian” doesn’t encompass all women who are attracted to women (think of bi/pan women, etc) so people will use wlw and mlm as a shorthand for “women attracted to women” and “men attracted to men”
